factoryFeedback: Competitor research must capture presentation topology: world-space vs screen-space, attachment object, timing of value growth, and occlusion order.
A UI feature is not accepted merely because a DOM node, state field or count exists; QA must prove the signal is attached to the correct object and visible at the causal moment.
The design contract must distinguish persistent HUD economy from per-cut world reward and finish-wall brick rewards.
Reference media identity verification must happen before any timeline sampling or competitor inference.
nextDecision: Do not make further visual patches until the correct target recording is reattached or the human-approved reference contract explicitly locks the world-space reward topology.
